neighbours.label: ' to' right after a naming or treating verb ('was named to', 'were treated to'; also 'view themselves to be', 'pictured to himself'), not the 'to' of motion or a plain infinitive; the − pole is the matching ' as' after 'refer to him / address him'
fire: Two years later she was named to the Supreme Court by the president.
The children were treated to ice cream after the school play.
In March he was named to the all-star team for the third time.
Visitors are treated to a view of the whole valley from the terrace.
The young lawyer was named to head the new department.
The crowd was treated to a brilliant display of fireworks.
The senator was named to the finance committee last week.
The winners were treated to lunch by the mayor.
quiet: Two years later she was named as the president's choice for the court.
The children walked to the shop for ice cream after the school play.
In March he wanted to join the all-star team for the third time.
Visitors climb to the terrace for a view of the whole valley.
The young lawyer was called the head of the new department.
The crowd went to see a brilliant display of fireworks.
The senator was described as an expert on finance last week.
The winners had lunch with the mayor and returned to work.

notes: Probes: named to 1.16-1.24, treated to 0.87-0.88, view/consider themselves to be 0.47-0.88, appointed/promoted to 0.22-0.30, walked to / used to 0.01-0.04.
